l1: Is the device prompting for a recovery key at boot?
Is the recovery key escrowed to Azure AD, AD, or Intune?
What triggered the recovery prompt, such as a firmware or boot change?
Is TPM present and enabled in the device's firmware settings?
Is this a Slate/tablet device where preboot keyboard input may not be available for PIN entry?
l2: What TPM version and PCR measurement profile is configured?
Is the encryption method AES-CBC (with or without Elephant Diffuser) or XTS-AES, and does it match compliance requirements?
Was Secure Boot or firmware settings recently changed on this device?
Is the device using TPM-only, TPM+PIN, or TPM+startup key protectors?
Is this environment using MBAM (Microsoft BitLocker Administration and Monitoring) for centralized recovery key storage?

l1: Run 'manage-bde -status' to check protection status on all volumes.
Check Settings > Privacy & Security > Device Encryption for status.
Confirm TPM status via 'tpm.msc' or 'Get-Tpm' in PowerShell.
Check whether the recovery key ID matches one in Azure AD or AD.
Run 'Get-Tpm | Out-File C:\TPM.txt' to capture TPM version and status (not supported on Windows 7).
l2: Run 'Get-BitLockerVolume' for full protector and key protector detail.
If multiple protectors are configured (e.g. recovery key + external key), confirm both decrypt to the same Volume Master Key (VMK) — a mismatch indicates decryption failure.
Check the BitLocker-API event log for suspension or lockout events.
Query Azure AD device record for the escrowed BitLocker key via Intune.

l1: Enter the recovery key retrieved from the user's Microsoft account or AD.
Confirm the correct recovery key ID is being used, not a stale one.
Check for recent firmware, BIOS, or boot order changes causing the prompt.
Suspend BitLocker before planned firmware updates to avoid future prompts.

For Slate/tablet devices requiring preboot auth, ensure the policy 'Enable use of BitLocker authentication requiring preboot keyboard input on slates' is enabled — otherwise PIN/password protectors can lock the device out.
If encryption progress is stuck at a fixed percentage, check disk health (SMART status) since a failing drive can stall the encryption pass.
Confirm whether Used Space Only or Full Encryption was selected — Used Space Only completes far faster and a 'stuck' report may just be a misunderstanding of expected duration.
l2: Clear and re-seal the TPM if repeated unexplained recovery prompts occur.
Re-escrow the recovery key to Azure AD or AD if it is missing.
Rebuild key protectors with 'manage-bde -protectors -add' after remediation.
If a 'clear key' condition is suspected (VMK stored unencrypted), re-enable full protection and rotate protectors immediately.

For advanced consultation on BitLocker internals, Microsoft's internal BitLocker engineering team maintains a discussion alias — escalate persistent/unclear cases through your normal escalation path rather than guessing at undocumented behavior.

l1: Record the recovery key ID displayed on the prompt screen.
Note the exact trigger event, such as BIOS update or docking change.
Confirm where the recovery key is expected to be escrowed.
Capture the output of 'manage-bde -status' before remediation.
Run 'manage-bde -status > C:\BDEStatus.txt' for a general encryption status export, and confirm TPM is listed under All Key Protectors.
l2: Export 'Get-BitLockerVolume' output for all volumes and protectors.
Collect BitLocker-API and TPM event logs around the time of the prompt.
Pull the Azure AD or AD BitLocker recovery key object for verification.
Note the configured encryption method (AES-CBC 128/256 or XTS-AES 128/256) for compliance review.

unexpected_recovery_prompt.title: Unexpected BitLocker recovery key prompt at boot

steps.action: Confirm the exact recovery key ID shown on screen
steps.expect: Key ID is legible and recorded

steps.action: Check Azure AD or AD for a matching escrowed key with that ID
steps.expect: Matching recovery key object is found

steps.action: Enter the recovery key to boot the device
Investigate and remediate the root trigger, such as a firmware change
Reboot the device once more to confirm no repeat prompt
steps.expect: Device boots normally without a recovery prompt

recovery_key_unknown_mbam_lookup.title: User at recovery prompt doesn't know where to find their recovery key

steps.action: Confirm the machine is genuinely stuck at the BitLocker recovery prompt and note the recovery key ID shown
steps.expect: Key ID is legible and recorded

steps.action: Determine whether the environment escrows keys to Azure AD/AD, or uses MBAM for centralized recovery
steps.expect: Identifies the correct lookup path for this environment

steps.action: If MBAM is in use, retrieve the key via the MBAM Self-Service Portal, or have the Helpdesk pull it from the MBAM recovery and hardware database
steps.expect: Matching recovery key is located and provided to the user

steps.action: Otherwise, retrieve the key from the user's Microsoft account or the escrowed AD/Azure AD object using the key ID
steps.expect: Matching recovery key is located and provided to the user

steps.action: Enter the recovery key and confirm the device boots successfully
steps.expect: Device boots into Windows without a repeat prompt

tpm_owner_lockout_after_failed_attempts.title: TPM enters lockout after repeated failed PIN/authorization attempts

steps.action: Run 'Get-Tpm' and check the LockoutCount / IsLockedOut properties
steps.expect: Confirms the TPM is actually in a lockout state, not a different failure

steps.action: Determine the TPM's configured lockout recovery time and whether an owner password/clear is required
steps.expect: Identifies whether waiting it out or a manual clear is the right path

steps.action: Wait out the lockout duration, or if urgent, use 'tpm.msc' > Clear TPM (requires physical presence/reboot) as a last resort — note this can require BitLocker recovery afterward
steps.expect: TPM lockout clears and normal authentication resumes

steps.action: Re-check 'Get-Tpm' and attempt normal PIN entry
steps.expect: TPM accepts the correct PIN without further lockout

encryption_stuck_at_percentage.title: BitLocker encryption progress appears stuck at a fixed percentage

steps.action: Run 'manage-bde -status' and confirm the percentage hasn't moved over a reasonable observation window
steps.expect: Confirms a genuine stall versus a slow but progressing full-disk encryption pass

steps.action: Check disk health (SMART) and confirm whether Full Encryption (slower) rather than Used Space Only was selected
steps.expect: Identifies whether this is expected behavior or a genuine disk/hardware issue

steps.action: If disk health is poor, back up data and plan for disk replacement rather than continuing to force encryption
steps.expect: Avoids data loss from continuing to encrypt a failing disk

steps.action: If disk health is fine, pause and resume encryption ('manage-bde -pause'/'-resume C:') to nudge the process
